briefs.flowNote: Money is going into defensives and banks: financials (XLF +0.4%), real estate (XLRE +0.4%), staples (XLP +0.4%), health care (XLV +0.2%) and communication (XLC +0.3%) are the only green sectors after the hot CPI. bigPicture: A hot core CPI on top of Waller's hike talk puts the market's main worry, a December hike, back in charge; rate-sensitive AI and small caps fall first.
Yesterday's +7% chip rally looked like capitulation, but one day does not make a bottom; today checks whether it survives higher rate odds.
Defensives and banks are the only sectors bid: XLF, XLRE, XLP and XLV are green and have led over the past month.
Cheaper oil (Brent −2.7%) eases one inflation channel but did not stop core from beating; energy keeps losing money (XLE −7.9% over 5 days).
snapshot.takeaway: The CPI result is known; what matters now is the Fed's response. A hot core with Waller already talking 50 bp makes the leveraged AI names (CRWV tonight) and yesterday's chip bounce the most exposed. Banks and defensives are the side money is choosing. Let the first 15 minutes and the 2-year yield set direction before trusting any premarket gap.

sectors.text: After yesterday's ~7% SOX rally, the hot core print hits the highest-beta names: MU −3.0%, AMD −2.1%, AVGO −2.0%, NVDA −1.5% (FBI probe), TSM −0.7% despite October sales +59.7%. SMH −2.1% premarket.

Hyperscalers hold up (AMZN −0.2%), but the debt-funded names fall on the hike risk: CRWV −3.1% before tonight's report, NBIS −2.8% before Thursday's. Bernstein raised its view of Oracle's AI opportunity.
Power and cooling give back part of yesterday's CEG-driven rally: VRT −4.7%, CEG −2.8% with no new news. Sanmina +10.9% on a FY27 guide well above estimates shows server builders still have orders.

IGV −0.5% before the print and −8.8% over a month; high-multiple software is on the report's losing side of a hike. IBM and Microsoft announced an industry AI agent platform; Qualys −7% on its outlook.

Brent fell below $90 for the first time since August (90.11, −2.7%; WTI 84.92) on Trump's 'fairly soon' Iran comment. Refiners lead the drop (VLO −2.5%, MPC −1.7%); OXY beat but trades −1.3%. XLE −7.9% over 5 days.
Banks are the report's winners if the Fed signals a December hike: XLF +0.4% after the print, JPM +0.9%. Diamondback and KKR agreed to buy Deep Blue Midland Basin.
